name: Simple Mortgage Calculator
author: Mortgage Calculator

sections.description:
Simple Mortgage Calculator adds a small, clean mortgage calculator to your site. Visitors enter the home price, down payment, interest rate and loan term, and see their estimated monthly payment straight away, without a page reload. Add it with the “Simple Mortgage Calculator” block, use it as a sidebar widget or put it inside a page or post with a shortcode.

Features

  • Four inputs: home price, interest rate, term in years and down payment
  • Instant monthly payment result in the browser
  • Sidebar widget with a custom title and currency symbol
  • “Simple Mortgage Calculator” block for the block editor
  • [mortgage_calc] shortcode for pages and posts, with an optional currency attribute
  • Clean flat styling for the widget; its fields adapt to the width of the sidebar
  • Translation-ready
  • No settings page and no account needed

How to use

As a block: in the block editor click the (+) button, search for “Simple Mortgage Calculator” and insert it. The sidebar has the currency symbol.

As a shortcode: add this to any page or post (optionally [mortgage_calc currency="€"]).

[mortgage_calc]

As a widget: go to Appearance > Widgets and add “Simple Mortgage Calculator” to a sidebar or widget area. You can set the widget title and the currency symbol shown in the field hints and the result.

How the payment is calculated

The calculator uses the standard amortization formula for a fixed-rate loan: the loan amount is the home price minus the down payment, and the monthly payment is calculated from the monthly interest rate (annual rate divided by 12) and the number of monthly payments (term in years times 12). The result covers principal and interest only.

Who it is for

Real-estate agents, home-buying blogs, mortgage brokers and any site that wants to give visitors a quick payment estimate.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the /ct-mortgage-calculator/ folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the Simple Mortgage Calculator plugin through the “Plugins” menu in WordPress.
  3. Insert the “Simple Mortgage Calculator” block, add the widget under Appearance > Widgets, or paste the shortcode [mortgage_calc] into a page or post.
  4. And you’re good to go!
sections.faq:
How do I add the calculator to a page?

In the block editor insert the “Simple Mortgage Calculator” block. Or paste the shortcode [mortgage_calc] into the page or post (in the block editor, into a Shortcode block).

Can I use it as a sidebar widget?

Yes. Add “Simple Mortgage Calculator” under Appearance > Widgets and choose a title and currency symbol.

How is the monthly payment calculated?

With the standard fixed-rate amortization formula, using the home price minus the down payment as the loan amount, the annual interest rate divided by 12 and the term in years times 12 payments.

Does the result include property tax, insurance or PMI?

No. The result is principal and interest only. Taxes, home insurance, PMI and fees are not included, so the real monthly cost will be higher. The calculator gives an estimate, not a loan offer.

Can I change the currency or colors?

The widget and the block have a currency field, and the shortcode accepts currency="€"; the default is a dollar sign. The widget styling lives in the plugin stylesheet (assets/style.css) and can be overridden with your own CSS. The shortcode form mostly inherits your theme’s form styles.

Does the plugin send visitors’ data anywhere?

No. The calculation runs in the visitor’s browser and the numbers entered are not saved or sent to a server.

1.5.0

  • New: Gutenberg block “Simple Mortgage Calculator” with a currency setting.
  • New: the [mortgage_calc] shortcode accepts a currency attribute.
  • New: the plugin is translation-ready; the screen-reader labels and the error message of the calculator can be translated too.
  • New: a review reminder in the admin after two weeks, dismissible.

1.4.2

  • Security: escape all output; the widget title and currency are now sanitized when saved and escaped when printed.
  • Security: shortcode field labels are escaped inside the inline focus/blur handlers.
  • Text domain changed to the plugin slug; internal functions and the widget class use a unique prefix (saved widgets are unaffected).
